statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of the public downloader, a specialized downloader, an article, successful core flow, and HTTP failure state.

page.notes: Root redirects to /en2. Public ad-supported TikTok download utility with localized variants.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for respects-color-scheme
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture: white navigation/content and the same bright blue hero remain. The DOM CSS hard-codes #fff surfaces and contains no prefers-color-scheme rule.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for respects-reduced-motion
checkOutcomes.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, the probe found 30 sampled elements still transitioning for 86–200 ms, including the menu, loader wrapper, and every FAQ accordion; no reduced-motion override was present.
Lighthouse and the prefers-contrast screenshot directly tested text/control visibility.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for view-transitions
checkOutcomes.evidence: The DOM and interaction probe show no view-transition usage; successful submission replaces the primary view with the video result and download actions as an abrupt state swap.
No scroll-linked animation or scrollytelling surface exists on the audited templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked animation or scrollytelling surface exists on the audited templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No gesture-driven carousel, swipe, drag, or pull interaction exists in the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No gesture-driven carousel, swipe, drag, or pull interaction exists in the representative paths.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for scroll-state-aware-chrome
checkOutcomes.evidence: The article is 5,034 CSS px tall at mobile width, while its static header has no progress, sticky state, or scroll-state styling; DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll timeline or scroll-state query.
No tooltip or edge-positioned popover was present in the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip or edge-positioned popover was present in the representative paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Clear H1, labeled navigation, article hierarchy, and result actions preserve orientation.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for no-intrusive-interruptions
checkOutcomes.evidence: The captured overlay covers the entire viewport and takes focus before the primary task. It exposes “Consent” and “Manage options” but no equivalent one-click rejection on the first layer.
The consent UI exposes role=dialog and focus; FAQs use native buttons, with no unlabeled overlay div found.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for reduced-chrome
checkOutcomes.evidence: The 360×800 homepage and slideshow captures reserve roughly half the first viewport as blank ad space between the downloader and useful content; the desktop capture also gives a large dark ad box priority.
Layout measured 0 px horizontal overflow at 360 px on home and article.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for component-level-responsiveness
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page does reflow without overflow, but DOM/CSS inspection found zero @container rules while reusable downloader, card, footer, and navigation components rely on global 769/1024/1216/1400px media queries.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for input-modality-aware
checkOutcomes.evidence: After programmatically focusing the URL input, computed style was outline: none 0px and box-shadow: none. The stylesheet explicitly removes outlines from focused inputs.
First viewport clearly states TikTok Video Download and presents one URL field and Download action.
A public TikTok URL completed to titled media plus Download Video and Download Video HD actions.
Successful submission exposes a result state; a true 404 returns status 404, explains the failure, and links home.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for good-core-web-vitals
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.3 s, interactive 10.4 s, TBT 170 ms, and performance 0.69. HAR captured 1,158,193 transferred bytes, of which 1,129,262 bytes and 24/33 requests were third-party.
Layout observer measured CLS 0 on desktop and mobile; Lighthouse reported CLS 0.031.
Trace recorded zero long tasks and 0 ms TBT; Lighthouse TBT was 170 ms.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for efficient-resource-delivery
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.3 s, interactive 10.4 s, TBT 170 ms, and performance 0.69. HAR captured 1,158,193 transferred bytes, of which 1,129,262 bytes and 24/33 requests were third-party.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for trim-unused-and-duplicate-code
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 623 KiB unused JS across seven resources, including ad, prebid, HLS, IMA, analytics, and consent scripts; estimated LCP savings were 3.36 s.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for names-roles-labels
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found both Android and iOS app links in the tab order with no screen-reader-visible text, aria-label, labelledby, or title. The main URL field is only named generically “Name”.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for sufficient-contrast
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse/axe reported four serious failures: the Download button is 2.45:1, Search is 3.66:1, and consent text/links are 1.82:1 and 2.8:1. The high-contrast capture also renders the consent surface with effectively invisible labels.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for structure-and-focus
checkOutcomes.evidence: After programmatically focusing the URL input, computed style was outline: none 0px and box-shadow: none. The stylesheet explicitly removes outlines from focused inputs.
Mobile captures show readable 16 px body text, clear headings, and no clipping across home/article.
Viewport allows maximum-scale=5; 360 px captures reflow without overflow and primary controls are 48 px tall.
Lighthouse errors-in-console audit passed and no uncaught error was observed in the valid core flow.
DOM has HTML doctype, UTF-8 charset, valid viewport; image primitive found no rendered img defects.
Lighthouse best-practices scored 1.0 and inspector-issues/errors-in-console passed; no permission prompt appeared.
Home and specialized pages expose descriptive unique titles and meta descriptions.
40/40 inspected links have hrefs, robots permits indexing, viewport exists, and mobile has no overflow.
HTTP 200 content has canonical /en2, index/follow, 24 hreflang alternates, robots and sitemap entries.
Three JSON-LD blocks plus Open Graph and Twitter metadata describe the visible public utility.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for secure-transport-and-headers
checkOutcomes.evidence: Headers probe found no CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. All six cookies lacked Secure; three analytics cookies also used SameSite=None and 400-day expiry.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for data-minimisation-and-third-parties
checkOutcomes.evidence: Tracker probe observed 13 third-party origins and known Google Analytics, DoubleClick, and Tag Manager trackers. HAR recorded 24 third-party requests and 1.13 MB third-party transfer; the CMP says data may be shared with 220 partners and precise geolocation may be used.
The public downloader has no authentication flow and no browser permission request in the tested paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: The public downloader has no authentication flow and no browser permission request in the tested paths.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for defensive-browser-policies
checkOutcomes.evidence: Headers probe found no CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. All six cookies lacked Secure; three analytics cookies also used SameSite=None and 400-day expiry.
Discoverability found 86% raw-HTML content coverage with title, H1, and description present; not a JS shell.
Core submission completed and the consent dialog retained focus without a blank/broken shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for offline-and-installable
checkOutcomes.evidence: The DOM probe found no web app manifest and no controlling service worker. This is an app-like utility with a repeated core action, so an installable shell and an explanatory offline state are applicable even though downloading itself requires connectivity.
A genuine 404 responds 404 with a clear explanation and homepage recovery link.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for lang-dir-and-logical-properties
checkOutcomes.evidence: The site exposes 24 hreflang alternates including Arabic, but the English page has no dir and source inspection counted 54 physical left/right declarations versus zero logical inline/block declarations.
The representative pages display no dates, numbers, currencies, durations, or calendar data requiring locale formatting.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative pages display no dates, numbers, currencies, durations, or calendar data requiring locale formatting.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The representative pages contain no event or time-zone-dependent data.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative pages contain no event or time-zone-dependent data.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for no-dark-patterns
checkOutcomes.evidence: The blocking first-layer CMP offers “Consent” and “Manage options” while omitting an equally prominent reject action, despite describing 220 partners and precise-geolocation use.
The tested 404 explains the issue without blame and provides a direct route home.
The URL input uses type=text, required, placeholder guidance, and the successful flow did not discard entered context.
No purchase, subscription, billing, account closure, or authentication flow exists.
checkOutcomes.reason: No purchase, subscription, billing, account closure, or authentication flow exists.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for optimised-assets
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 623 KiB unused JS across seven resources, including ad, prebid, HLS, IMA, analytics, and consent scripts; estimated LCP savings were 3.36 s.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for no-wasteful-work
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 623 KiB unused JS across seven resources, including ad, prebid, HLS, IMA, analytics, and consent scripts; estimated LCP savings were 3.36 s.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct browser evidence and guidance-backed review for third-party-and-media-budget
checkOutcomes.evidence: Tracker probe observed 13 third-party origins and known Google Analytics, DoubleClick, and Tag Manager trackers. HAR recorded 24 third-party requests and 1.13 MB third-party transfer; the CMP says data may be shared with 220 partners and precise geolocation may be used.
Server-rendered content, JSON-LD, canonical URLs, and a semantic GET form expose the primary capability to agents without proprietary UI automation.
The site has no inference feature for which on-device model execution would be appropriate.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site has no inference feature for which on-device model execution would be appropriate.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Twenty FAQ toggles produced a 22,515,627-byte heap versus 22,559,684 bytes in the comparable consent-loaded snapshot, with no retained growth signal.
Comparable loaded heaps remained about 22.5 MB after repeated interaction; constructor populations were stable.
Heap summaries showed no Detached* constructor among top retained constructors and repeated toggles did not increase closure count materially (26,285 to 26,288).

paths.description: Primary downloader landing page and shared site shell; tested desktop/mobile, preferences, security, network, accessibility, discoverability, and memory.
Specialized slideshow downloader representing alternate utility templates.
Long-form instructional content template, selected from sitemap.
End-to-end primary flow using a public TikTok URL through media result and download choices.
Nonexistent route representing HTTP failure and recovery.

findings.summary: The page declares dark color-scheme support but remains a hard-coded light interface.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture: white navigation/content and the same bright blue hero remain. The DOM CSS hard-codes #fff surfaces and contains no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Use color-scheme: light dark plus prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens for page, navigation, cards, text, fields, and overlays.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion users still receive all component transitions.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, the probe found 30 sampled elements still transitioning for 86–200 ms, including the menu, loader wrapper, and every FAQ accordion; no reduced-motion override was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or sharply shorten non-essential transitions and animations inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: Primary controls and consent content fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe reported four serious failures: the Download button is 2.45:1, Search is 3.66:1, and consent text/links are 1.82:1 and 2.8:1. The high-contrast capture also renders the consent surface with effectively invisible labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose foreground/background pairs meeting at least 4.5:1, and test the CMP under prefers-contrast and forced-colors.

findings.summary: The downloader swaps from form to result without spatial continuity.
findings.evidence: The DOM and interaction probe show no view-transition usage; successful submission replaces the primary view with the video result and download actions as an abrupt state swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the form-to-result state change in a same-document View Transition, with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-aware orientation.
findings.evidence: The article is 5,034 CSS px tall at mobile width, while its static header has no progress, sticky state, or scroll-state styling; DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll timeline or scroll-state query.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight article progress indicator or compact sticky navigation using declarative scroll-driven styling.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent interstitial blocks the downloader on load.
findings.evidence: The captured overlay covers the entire viewport and takes focus before the primary task. It exposes “Consent” and “Manage options” but no equivalent one-click rejection on the first layer.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface with equally prominent accept/reject choices and defer non-essential vendors until a choice.

findings.summary: Reserved advertising space dominates the mobile path.
findings.evidence: The 360×800 homepage and slideshow captures reserve roughly half the first viewport as blank ad space between the downloader and useful content; the desktop capture also gives a large dark ad box priority.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse empty ad slots, reserve only known creative dimensions when an ad is available, and keep task-supporting content adjacent to the form.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is coupled entirely to viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The page does reflow without overflow, but DOM/CSS inspection found zero @container rules while reusable downloader, card, footer, and navigation components rely on global 769/1024/1216/1400px media queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Define containment for reusable components and use size container queries where their layout depends on available component width.

findings.summary: The primary text field has no visible keyboard focus indicator.
findings.evidence: After programmatically focusing the URL input, computed style was outline: none 0px and box-shadow: none. The stylesheet explicitly removes outlines from focused inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible outline or ring and never remove focus indication without an equivalent replacement.

findings.summary: Mobile loading is slow and dominated by advertising JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.3 s, interactive 10.4 s, TBT 170 ms, and performance 0.69. HAR captured 1,158,193 transferred bytes, of which 1,129,262 bytes and 24/33 requests were third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep advertising and analytics off the critical path, load them only after consent and user-visible content, and prioritize the downloader UI.

findings.summary: The initial page ships hundreds of KiB of unused third-party JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 623 KiB unused JS across seven resources, including ad, prebid, HLS, IMA, analytics, and consent scripts; estimated LCP savings were 3.36 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant vendors and conditionally import ad/video libraries only when the corresponding feature and consent state require them.

findings.summary: App-store links have no accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found both Android and iOS app links in the tab order with no screen-reader-visible text, aria-label, labelledby, or title. The main URL field is only named generically “Name”.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each icon link a descriptive accessible name and replace the URL field’s generic aria-label with a visible label such as “TikTok video URL”.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security controls and cookie flags are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers probe found no CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. All six cookies lacked Secure; three analytics cookies also used SameSite=None and 400-day expiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP and HSTS, add restrictive referrer/permissions policies, and set Secure plus appropriate SameSite and retention on every cookie.

findings.summary: The page contacts a large advertising and analytics surface before an explicit choice.
findings.evidence: Tracker probe observed 13 third-party origins and known Google Analytics, DoubleClick, and Tag Manager trackers. HAR recorded 24 third-party requests and 1.13 MB third-party transfer; the CMP says data may be shared with 220 partners and precise geolocation may be used.
findings.suggestedFix: Default-deny non-essential vendors until consent, reduce the vendor list, remove precise-geolocation purposes, and audit every retained endpoint against necessity.

findings.summary: The app-like downloader is neither installable nor prepared for offline failure.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no web app manifest and no controlling service worker. This is an app-like utility with a repeated core action, so an installable shell and an explanatory offline state are applicable even though downloading itself requires connectivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a manifest and service worker that caches the shell and presents an explicit offline/retry state for the network-dependent download action.

findings.summary: Localized pages are not built with bidirectional layout primitives.
findings.evidence: The site exposes 24 hreflang alternates including Arabic, but the English page has no dir and source inspection counted 54 physical left/right declarations versus zero logical inline/block declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir per locale and migrate directional spacing, positioning, and borders to logical properties; test the Arabic route in RTL.

findings.summary: Consent choice is asymmetric and encourages acceptance.
findings.evidence: The blocking first-layer CMP offers “Consent” and “Manage options” while omitting an equally prominent reject action, despite describing 220 partners and precise-geolocation use.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Reject all beside Accept all with equal visual weight, use plain purpose language, and make withdrawal as easy as acceptance.

taskList.title: Replace the blocking asymmetric CMP with equal Accept all and Reject all actions, and default-deny non-essential vendors until choice.
Remove redundant ad/video vendors and load remaining third-party JavaScript only after consent and outside the critical path.
Fix control/CMP contrast, restore visible focus, and add descriptive names to app links and the URL field.
Deploy CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and correct Secure/SameSite cookie flags.
Collapse empty ad slots so useful content follows the downloader immediately.
Implement preference-driven dark mode and a reduced-motion override.
Add component container queries and migrate directional CSS to logical properties with RTL testing.
Add an installable shell, offline explanation, and retry state.
Add subtle result View Transitions and article scroll orientation with reduced-motion fallback.
